about: Step 3B PR 6 answer key (tests/delivery/expected/traces.json), written by the controller by hand before the code, by reading the committed synthetic new-format handoffs under rulings D1, D4, D5, D11, S6 and 6-1 to 6-15 (pr6-rulings.md) the PR 6 mutation gaps M1, M2 and ruling 6-16. Each case builds every module from `fixtures` + `file` after its text replacements (each `old` occurs exactly once; apply in order) and calls the builder with the modules in order and `as_of`. `expect` holds some or all of `traces`, `table`, `jump`, `items`; each given part is compared whole. A value cell's `at` is a decimal string compared as Decimal(at) == the built Decimal. `refused`: DeliveryRefused. Every name is invented. Implementers do not edit this file.

rows.item: Creditors are exposed to refinancing risk rather than to weak earnings: net debt of USD 1,390 million is 4.2x earnings, and the next maturities fall inside two years.

rows.item: Leverage is moderate but not low, at 4.2x net debt to EBITDA, so there is little room for an earnings miss.
A large part of the debt comes due soon: 38% of gross debt matures within 24 months, which makes refinancing access the deciding factor.
Liquidity support rests on an undrawn revolver that steps down, which narrows the cushion over time.

The strongest evidence against concern is the consistent earnings record over recent quarters. A signed refinancing of the nearest maturity would move the view towards comfort. The company has not said how it intends to fund the step-down.
Peer leverage was not compared, so the 4.2x reading has no market anchor.
